terms.comment: Classically an admission; in the Church the confession of sins, and the sacrament itself, which both churches keep: the Greek and Slavonic churches also call it the mystery of repentance (μετάνοια), the Latin Church the sacrament of penance (paenitentia). To confess is peccāta cōnfitērī; to hear confessions, cōnfessiōnēs audīre (Morgan–Owens).
Tertullian’s Greek word, ἐξομολόγησις, for the confession made in penance.

phrases.latin: Sī cōnfiteāmur peccāta nostra: fidēlis est, et jūstus, ut remittat nōbīs peccāta nostra
phrases.english: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins

phrases.latin: Cōnfitēminī ergō alterutrum peccāta vestra, et ōrāte prō invicem ut salvēminī
phrases.english: So confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed

sources: Lewis & Short: confessio · Lewis & Short: confiteor · Lewis & Short: exomologesis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. confession; hear confessions.
